text: . To further strengthen community participation in India’s fight against tuberculosis (TB), the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare will launch JOSH (Joint Squad for Health) Teams in New Delhi tomorrow. The initiative to be launched by Health and Family Welfare Minister J P Nadda seeks to enable young people to become active partners in the TB response, providing them with a defined platform to contribute to awareness generation, social mobilisation and community engagement.In the first phase, JOSH Teams will be rolled out across 55 districts in 11 States, with the objective of strengthening youth-led community mobilisation and taking the message of TB Mukt Bharat to the grassroots. Mr Nadda will lead the national launch of JOSH Teams in the presence of Youth Affairs and Sports Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya.The event will bring together senior leadership and stakeholders from the participating Ministries, elected representatives, MY Bharat Volunteers, NCC Cadets and other stakeholders associated with India’s TB elimination efforts. In the first phase, the initiative will focus on strengthening engagement at the Block and community levels, taking the TB Mukt Bharat message beyond health facilities and closer to people and communities where they live, work and interact. JOSH Teams will support the dissemination of key messages on TB symptoms, prevention, timely diagnosis and completion of treatment.

. India has rejected the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation’s (OIC) remarks on Jammu and Kashmir and India’s actions against terror infrastructure in Pakistan. Speaking at the UN General Assembly Sixth Committee, Lok Sabha MP Biplab Kumar Deb said those making the remarks were unable to distinguish between the victim and the perpetrator. He asserted that India has the right to defend its people against cross-border terrorism emanating from Pakistan.Mr Deb also rejected the OIC’s reference to Jammu and Kashmir. He said India’s experience shows that terrorism is a persistent threat and referred to the Pahalgam terror attack of April last year, in which 26 civilians were killed. He said terrorist groups continue to exploit emerging technologies for recruitment, radicalisation, propaganda, operational planning and terrorist financing. India also called for an early conclusion of the Comprehensive Convention on International Terrorism.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has emphasised that technology must become a tool for inclusive and sustainable development. Prime Minister Modi interacted with Global System for Mobile Communications Association (GSMA) Board members at Seva Teerth yesterday, ahead of the India Mobile Congress.The India Mobile Congress is scheduled to be held from the 7th to the 10th of this month in New Delhi. Mr Modi stressed that democratisation of technology is essential to ensure that no section of society is left behind. He emphasised the need to make technology and digital services affordable and accessible, particularly for the Global South, and highlighted the importance of taking technology to the last mile to prevent a widening digital divide.The Prime Minister highlighted the potential of Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) as a transformative force, particularly for developing countries. He noted that discussions on DPI with several world leaders had demonstrated its growing global relevance and said that such platforms can serve as a springboard for countries of the Global South.Addressing the growing challenge of digital and cyber fraud, Mr Modi said, the problem requires technology-driven solutions. He suggested sustained awareness messages for users to warn people about potential fraud calls. The Prime Minister also highlighted the need for global standards and common rules for emerging technologies. On the growing threat of deepfakes and AI-generated content, he suggested exploring mechanisms to allow users to immediately identify its origin.GSMA is a global organisation unifying the mobile ecosystem, representing mobile operators and organisations across the mobile ecosystem and adjacent industries. The GSMA Board members highlighted India’s emergence as a global leader in digital and mobile connectivity. They noted the rapid expansion of 4G and 5G, the scale of digital public infrastructure and the growth of the telecom and mobile manufacturing ecosystem.They hailed India’s investment-friendly policy framework and emphasised the role of secure, resilient and trusted digital infrastructure in supporting continued digital growth. The meeting was attended by Minister of Communications, Jyotiraditya Scindia, Minister of State for Communications, Dr. Pemmasani Chandra Sekhar, GSMA board members and senior officials of the government.

. In China Open Tennis, Serbian Novak Djokovic has stormed into the men’s singles final after Daniil Medvedev of Russia was defaulted during their semi-final clash in Beijing. The record six-time champion was serving for the match at 7-5, 5-3, 15/15 when a ball rebounded off the back wall. Medvedev instinctively struck the ball, sending it into the crowd where it hit a spectator, resulting in his default. Djokovic has now reached his first ATP 500 final since winning the title in Astana in 2022. He will face fifth-seeded Australian Alex de Minaur today.

. External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar reached Accra, in Ghana, today. Sharing a social media post, the Minister appreciated the warm welcome by the Foreign Minister of Ghana Sam Okudzeto Ablakwa. Dr Jaishankar said, he looks forward to holding productive engagements to advance India-Ghana Comprehensive Partnership.

. External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar has said that India’s partnership with Africa is being built not just for today, but for generations to come. Addressing a gathering at the Foreign Service Institute of Ghana in Accra, he said diplomacy must manage competition without allowing it to turn into confrontation and promote cooperation despite differences in interests.Dr. Jaishankar highlighted India’s progress in the economy, infrastructure, digital technology and manufacturing. He stressed the need for India and Africa to turn their young populations into skilled and empowered citizens. He also underlined the importance of resilient supply chains for fuel, food, fertiliser and finance, and reaffirmed India’s commitment to strengthening the voice of the Global South.Dr. Jaishankar said India’s partnership with Africa covers trade, infrastructure, capacity building, humanitarian assistance and disaster relief, agriculture, health and clean energy. He also interacted with the Indian community and friends of India in Ghana. Later, he joined Ghanaian Foreign Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa and Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu in planting a Frangipani sapling under India’s ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ and Ghana’s ‘Tree for Life’ initiatives.

. Secretary (West) in the Ministry of External Affairs Sibi George received the National Security Advisor of Austria Dr. Peter Vorhofer. In a social media post, External Affairs Ministry said that they discussed ways to further strengthen India-Austria cooperation in security and strategic matters, including counter-terrorism and exchanged views on regional and global issues of mutual interest.

. The Union Cabinet has passed a resolution congratulating Prime Minister Narendra Modi for completing 25 years as the head of government. First, Mr Modi became the Chief Minister of Gujarat on 7th October 2001 and then became Prime Minister in 2014, and today he is completing 25 years as the head of government. Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said that Prime Minister Modi’s 25-year tenure is a testimony to the strength of Indian democracy.He said that a person from an ordinary family who dedicated himself to the service of the nation and is continuing to serve the country is a major example of the vitality, vibrancy and maturity of the democracy. Mr Vaishnaw said that Prime Minister Modi has created history that is unique in any democratic country. He said there are very few countries in the world where the people have repeatedly extended their support to a single leader. The minister said this support has been given because of his style of functioning, his right policies and his clear and good intentions.The Bharatiya Janata Party and Prime Minister Narendra Modi have always pursued public service, national service and the spirit of putting the nation first and the nation above all, with clear intentions and clear policies. The Minister highlighted ten major points of this Cabinet resolution.The first point is the expansion of the vision of development from Gujarat to the entire country. He said Prime Minister Narendra Modi introduced several changes in Gujarat through his programmes and policies, for which Mr Modi was honoured across the world. The Gujarat model was recognised and appreciated across the world and was subsequently implemented across India.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Andaman and Nicobar Islands, South Interior Karnataka and Uttarakhand tomorrow. It has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds over North Eastern parts of India, including Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura, during the next two days. According to IMD, Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Maharashtra, Marathwada, Odisha and Telangana are also likely to witness similar weather conditions tomorrow.

. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman today called on Swiss President Guy Parmelin in New Delhi. In a social media post, the Ministry of Finance said that both sides held discussions on issues of common interest to both India and Switzerland. They also held discussion of taking forward negotiations on the Bilateral Investment Treaty which is mutually beneficial to both nations with a view to enhance investment flows and deepening economic engagement.

. India and Uruguay will face each other today in a FIFA international friendly football match at the Yuva Bharati Krirangan in Salt Lake. India had earlier played out a 1-1 draw against Panama and suffered a 0-4 defeat to Brazil on Saturday. Learning from the mistakes of their previous match, the Indian team will be looking to put up a strong performance against two-time world champions Uruguay in their final friendly. India coach Khalid Jamil said there was a lack of coordination among the players in the last match. He said the players will remain alert from the very first minute against Uruguay.Uruguay coach Diego Forlán, meanwhile, said India have several skilled players capable of putting their opponents under pressure. He added that Uruguay are not taking the Indian team lightly.

. In Men’s Cricket, India will face West Indies in the first match of the five-match T20 International series at the Bharat Ratna Shri Atal Bihari Vajpayee Ekana Cricket Stadium in Lucknow today. The match will start at 7 PM IST. After winning gold at the 2026 Asian Games and a convincing 2-1 win in the One Day International series, the hosts will aim to continue their winning run against the West Indies. As many as 10 members of India’s Asian Games 2026 team have been picked for the series, while three players from the ODI squad are also part of the team. West Indies, on the other hand, have brought in a few power-packed reinforcements for the T20 International in the form of Shimron Hetmyer, Rovman Powell and Romario Shepherd. The next four T20 matches will be played in Ranchi, Indore, Hyderabad and Bengaluru on 9, 11, 14 and 17, of this month.

. The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas conducted a special inspection drive in Delhi to assess road dust and effectiveness of road cleaning operations across the city.The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has informed that the commission deployed four flying squad teams for the inspection which was carried out yesterday. The Flying Squad Teams inspected 25 road stretches covering approximately 35 kilometres of the Inner and Outer ring road which come under the jurisdiction of the Public Works Department (PWD), Delhi.The Ministry highlighted that the inspections, which were meant to seek strict implementation of road cleaning and dust mitigation measures, found 17 cases of violation. These violations include accumulation of construction and demolition waste and high visible road dust across inspected road stretches.CAQM has directed PWD, Delhi and other concerned agencies to take appropriate corrective measures to control road dust on priority basis. It also added the inspection shall continue under Operation Clean Air across Delhi-NCR to assess on-ground implementation of various air pollution abatement measures.

. United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres has warned member states about the consequences of failing to reform the UN Security Council. According to Deputy Spokesperson Farhan Haq, Guterres also encouraged the member nations to move forward with the stalled reform process. Haq made the remarks when asked about comments by External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar that the UN’s highest decision-making body must be reformed to remain relevant, given that UN membership has nearly quadrupled since the organisation was established in 1945. Haq said Guterres has consistently maintained that, as the United Nations has expanded, the Security Council must also expand and become more representative of the wider membership.

. The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) hasissued redalert for extremely heavy rainfall over isolated places of Chhattisgarh, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Telangana for the next two days. The Met Department has predicted heavy rainfall over Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Meghalaya, Bihar, Jharkhand, Kerala, Maharashtra, West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. The weather department also forecast thunderstorms accompanied with highly gusty winds over Madhya Pradesh and Parts of North-East tomorrow.For Delhi, IMD said the national capital will witness mostly clear skies with no rain. The maximum temperature in Delhi is expected to be around 34 to 35 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature of 23 to 25 degrees Celsius.

. Fighting intensified in Yemen today as the Saudi-led coalition carried out new operations against Houthi targets. The Saudi coalition said its naval forces conducted an operation in Hodeidah, destroying weapons depots, facilities storing explosive-laden boats and naval mines, and thwarting planned attacks on southern Red Sea waterways. It also said it destroyed a ballistic missile launch platform in Sanaa and a storage facility in Saada containing 20 missiles. The Houthi-affiliated media however, claimed that they had repelled advances by Saudi-backed forces in Dhubab and Bab Al Mandab. The latest exchanges follow the Yemeni government’s launch of Operation Dawn of Yemen, backed by Saudi airpower, to retake Houthi-held territory.Meanwhile, Bahrain’s Foreign Ministry expressed support for Saudi Arabia’s efforts to back Yemen’s internationally recognised government, restore state institutions and seek a comprehensive political solution.

. The World Bank has raised its forecast for India’s GDP growth in the current financial year to 7.1 per cent, up from 6.6 per cent projected in April. The revision follows stronger-than-expected growth, with the economy expanding 7.8 per cent in the first quarter of FY27, supported by robust private consumption and investment.The World Bank said private consumption is likely to remain the main growth driver, while stronger public investment and supportive financial and policy conditions will provide further support. Exports have also performed better than expected and are projected to offer a key upside to the growth outlook, although global trade and geopolitical uncertainties may weigh on private investment.On the supply side, industrial activity has exceeded expectations, with infrastructure and construction goods and electricity generation recording strong growth. However, a rainfall deficit during the southwest monsoon has weakened agricultural prospects and may moderately affect rural demand. The services sector, meanwhile, continues to register elevated growth despite moderating from last year’s high base.

. The country’s automobile retail sales rose 31.8 per cent year on year to over 25 lakh units in September this year, marking the best-ever first half of fiscal year, according to a report released by the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA).Passenger vehicle (PV) sales grew 32.1 per cent year on year in September, while commercial vehicle (CV) sales increased 37.6 per cent. Two-wheeler sales jumped 33 per cent, while three-wheeler sales rose 22 per cent over the same period.

. Belgian-born scientist Francis Halzen has won the Nobel Prize in Physics for his contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin.The 82-year-old Halzen led an international team that developed IceCube, a neutrino detector at the South Pole that has opened a new way of studying the universe. Neutrinos are tiny, nearly massless particles produced by stars and other cosmic events.The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences announced the award in Stockholm. The prize carries 12 million Swedish kronor, or about 1.2 million dollars.

. Himachal’s four women kabaddi players, including Pushpa Rana- captain of the Indian women’s kabaddi team that won the gold medal at Asian Games, today met Chief Minister Thakur Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu. During the meeting, the players requested that the government increase the prize money from rupees 33 lakhs to Rs. one crore and sought employment at the rank of DSP.Following the meeting, Rana stated that their primary demand was to raise the prize money to Rs. 1 crore. She mentioned that the Chief Minister responded positively to their requests and assured them that they would be fulfilled.On this occasion, Pushpa Rana also urged the youth to stay away from drugs and embrace sports. She remarked that sports not only pave the way for a better future but also inspire young people to lead healthy and disciplined lives.It is noteworthy that Himachal’s daughters, Pushpa Rana, Ritu Negi, Jyoti Thakur, and Bhavna Thakur, played a pivotal role in India’s golden victory at the Asian Games. The players expressed that the state government’s support would motivate them to deliver even better performances in the future.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices were trading over half a per cent up in the forenoon session today. The Sensex rose 462 points to 72,845, while the Nifty added 140 points to 22,696, when reports last came in. On the sectoral front, Power, Capital Goods and Oil and Gas emerged as the top gainers, while Hospitals, IT, and Realty led the decline.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall with isolated extremely heavy rainfall over Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand tomorrow. According to IMD, heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely over Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh tomorrow. The districts that are likely to receive heavy rainfall include Rampur, Pilibhit, Bareilly, Shahjahanpur and Bahraich. Meanwhile, districts of Madhya Pradesh which are expected to receive rainfall include Satna, Chhatarpur, Tikamgarh and Niwari.IMD said that the line of withdrawal of Southwest Monsoon continues to pass through Gurdaspur, Chandigarh, Muzaffarnagar, Aligarh, Dholpur, Udaipur, Deesa and Naliya.The Met Department has also predicted heavy rainfall over Delhi, Haryana, Chandigarh, Bihar, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Odisha, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim for the day. Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty windsare expectedto prevail over Punjab, Madhya Pradesh, Vidarbha, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Mahe, Telangana, Andaman and Nicobar Islands and parts of Northeast during the next two days.Meanwhile, parts of Delhi are expected to witness light to moderate rainfall tomorrow.

. Union Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu today said that the West Asia crisis is one of the major concerns, as it has put a significant burden leading to rise in aviation turbine fuel ATF prices. Talking to media in New Delhi, Mr. Naidu said that the government is in discussions with airlines and Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) regarding ATF prices to assess the situation. He said that the ministry will hold a meeting with all stakeholders and then take a decision.

. US President Donald Trump has said that he personally believes Iran was responsible for the terrorist attack carried out by an Omani co-pilot aboard a flydubai flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv. Trump said this while responding to media queries on the White House premises. The remarks came following the foiled mid-air hijacking and crash attempt aboard flydubai Flight FZ1073 on 30th of last month, when Omani co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami attacked Indian Captain Smit Machchhar inside the cockpit. The attack was thwarted after Captain Machchhar, despite being severely injured, succeeded in opening the cockpit door. The incident has drawn attention to the actions of Machchhar, who was praised by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as a hero of Israel, India, and the world.

. The India Meteorological Department IMD has forecast heavy rainfall over Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura today. It said thunderstorms with lightning and gusty winds is expected over Eastern and Western Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Haryana, Chandigarh, Delhi, and Himachal Pradesh today. Similar conditions are likely to prevail today in Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Kerala, Odisha, Punjab, Uttarakhand, West Bengal and Sikkim. The weatherman has forecast partly cloudy skies in the national capital, Delhi.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is completing 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into creation of the post of Chief of Defence Staff.Earlier, India’s three armed services – Army, Navy and the Air Force – planned, trained, procured and advised the government separately. Proposals for greater jointness had been made repeatedly since the Kargil Review Committee of 1999 and the Group of Ministers that followed it, but no single officer held authority across all three services. On the 15th of August 2019, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in his Independence Day address, announced the creation of the post of Chief of Defence Staff from the ramparts of the Red Fort. Prime Minister Modi said this will lead to better coordination among the three services.The Cabinet approved the decision in December 2019, along with a new Department of Military Affairs within the Ministry of Defence for the CDS to head.  Talking to Akashvani News, retired Lt General Sanjay Kulkarni said the appointment of CDS made it possible for the government to have one point of contact for advice on allmiltarymatters.After the formation of the post of CDS, all three forces have now got effective leadership at the top level.

. Members of the Asian Games Gold Medal winning Indian Hockey team landed at Amritsar airport to a rousing welcome today morning. They were greeted by enthusiastic citizens, sports fans, Punjab Hockey Association officials besides their parents with the drum beats, garlands and bouquets.Captain Harmanpreet, who scored two goals, expressed immense pride and joy at winning the Gold. He stated that winning and then retaining any title is the result of the collective effort and dedication of the entire team. He also underlined that securing a direct Olympic berth will prove to be very beneficial for the team, as they will now have ample time to assess their shortcomings and prepare for the Olympics. He also congratulated the Indian Women Hockey team as well for winning Gold in the Asian Games. Others who landed include Jugraj Singh, Hardik and Manpreet Singh.The Indian team won the historic Gold by defeating Malaysia by a comprehensive 5-1 margin and sealed the berth for Los Angeles Olympics- 2028 also.

. Home Minister Amit Shah today congratulated Prime Minister Narendra Modi on completing 25 years in public service. In a social media post, Mr Shah said that on this day in 2001, Mr Modi took the oath as Chief Minister of Gujarat and since then his continuous journey of relentless service, struggle, and dedication as Chief Minister and Prime Minister has become synonymous with the welfare of the poor, empowerment of women, upliftment of youth, and prosperity of every section of society.Mr Shah said that Prime Minister Modi has transformed the very definition of governance through implementation of people-centric policies, firmness in decision-making, transparency, and a guarantee of results, while establishing the ideal of politics of performance.The Home Minister said that as Gujarat Chief Minister, Mr Modi rebuilt the earthquake-ravaged Kutch, turning it into a model of reconstruction, through the Jyotigram Yojana. Mr Shah said that Mr Modi ensured 24-hour electricity reached every village, via solar energy and Vibrant Gujarat. The Home Minister said that he gave a new direction to investment and industry and achieved an over 8 per cent agricultural growth rate.The Home Minister also said that this same vision was expanded further by Mr Modi as Prime Minister. He said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Modi, India achieved new milestones from space to the seas, and from global forums to internal security. Mr Shah said that Mr Modi has instilled confidence in crores of countrymen, given the mantra of ‘Viksit Bharat’, and elicited a resolve to make India a leader in every sector by 2047.

. A 4.9-magnitude earthquake struck Uttarakhand’s Chamoli district on last night, sending tremors across several parts of the state and parts of Delhi-NCR. According to the National Centre for Seismology (NCS), the earthquake occurred at around 10:24 p.m., with its epicentre in Chamoli at a depth of approximately 13 km.Tremors were reported from Bageshwar, Pithoragarh, Champawat, Rudraprayag and Chamoli, while residents in Bhowali, Haldwani, Khatima, Rishikesh, Gopeshwar and Badrinath also felt the shaking. The tremors were strong enough to be noticed in parts of Delhi and the adjoining National Capital Region.The NCS confirmed the earthquake at around 10:40 p.m. The magnitude of an earthquake measures energy released at its source, while intensity refers to how strongly the shaking is experienced at a particular location. The level of shaking can vary depending on factors such as earthquake depth and local geological conditions.

. Foreign Portfolio Investor (FPI) flows turned negative in September after positive flows in July and August. According to the latest depository data, FPIs have offloaded Indian equities worth 35,861 crore rupees last month. Out of the total net outflows, 45,537 crore rupees were withdrawn through sales on stock exchanges, as geopolitical uncertainty, elevated US bond yields, and crude oil prices weighed on investors’ risk appetite. However, the trend of FPI investment through the primary market continued last month, with FPIs infusing 9,676 crore rupees in the primary market in September.Meanwhile, foreign investors also extended their selling to the debt market during the period under review. Last month, outflows from the debt securities through the Fully Accessible Route (FAR) stood at 10,431 crore rupees. FPIs withdrew 5,247 crore rupees through General Limit route and 5,049 crore rupees through Voluntary Retention Route (VRR).

. Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh has said that critical minerals are key to India’s energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. The Minister said this while addressing a special plenary of the 3rd Global Summit on Advanced Materials, Critical Minerals, and Metals in New Delhi. Dr Singh said that critical minerals and metals will be a driving component of the next phase of technological development, with their importance extending beyond mining to energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. He said that the global economy is undergoing a paradigm shift, with clean energy, electric mobility, semiconductors, telecommunications, aerospace, defence and nuclear energy emerging as major drivers of technological and industrial transformation. He added, India is now participating in this global discourse with much greater confidence and is preparing to assume a larger global role.Dr. Singh has called for early industry linkage with research and innovation, saying potential industry partners should be brought on board right from the beginning. He further said that a healthy synergy among research, industry, government and the non-government sector is essential for sustaining startups and entrepreneurs. The Minister also highlighted on building domestic capabilities for energy security as the world moves towards cleaner and greener sources of energy. He said that India’s next phase of growth in strategic technologies and materials will depend on working together of all stakeholders.

. Vice President C.P. Radhakrishnan has greeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi on completing 25 years of service to the Nation as Head of Government. In a social media post, Mr Radhakrishnan said, Mr Modi’s journey as Pradhan Sevak has transformed the vision of inclusive development into a nationwide mission, guided by Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas, and Sabka Prayaas. He said, across his visits to States and Union Territories, he has witnessed Bharat’s visible transformation through improved connectivity, digital advancement, expanding opportunities and inclusive development.The Vice President said, the greatest achievement of Mr Modi’s visionary leadership is liberating 25 crore people from extreme poverty. He said, it is a landmark historical achievement that human history can never forget. Mr Radhakrishnan hoped that the Almighty will bless Mr Modi with good health, happiness and strength as he continues to serve Bharat on its journey towards an inclusive, prosperous and Viksit Bharat by 2047.

. Athletes from the Army Sports Institute (ASI), Pune, won 12 medals at the Asian Games, accounting for 60 per cent of the 20 medals won by Indian Army athletes. A total of 25 ASI athletes were part of the Indian contingent.In Athletics, Gulveer Singh won three medals, including silver in the 1,500 and 10,000 metres and bronze in the 5,000 metres. Sawan Barwal won silver in the marathon, while Sarvesh Kushare secured silver in the high jump. Dharmveer was part of the bronze-winning 4×400 metre relay team.In Boxing, Sub Ankush won gold, while Sub Narender and Hav Kapil won bronze. In Archery, Sub Dhiraj secured two silver medals and set an Asian record with a score of 698 out of 720. Sub Deepak Punia won bronze in the 97-kilogram freestyle wrestling event. The performance highlights the Army Sports Institute’s sustained efforts in athlete development, specialist coaching, sports science and infrastructure under the Army’s Mission Olympics programme.

. In Ladakh, RNU Akashvani Kargil has launched a special podcast series under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, with the first programme focusing on “Natural Farming – Towards Sustainable and Climate-Resilient Agriculture.”The programme featured Dr. Nazir Hussain, Scientist, Krishi Vigyan Kendra Kargil, in conversation with Anayat Ali of RNU Akashvani Kargil.During the podcast, Dr. Nazir Hussain explained the principles of natural farming and highlighted its role in improving soil health, reducing dependence on external chemical inputs and promoting sustainable and climate-resilient agriculture.He discussed various aspects of the National Mission on Natural Farming, including chemical-free cultivation, livestock integration, diversified cropping, use of locally available bio-inputs and integration of traditional agricultural knowledge with scientific practices.Dr. Hussain said natural farming has considerable potential in Ladakh and Kargil, where agriculture is characterised by a short growing season, cold climatic conditions and limited water availability. He stressed the need for locally adapted practices, scientific research, farmer training and awareness for its successful adoption in the region.Comparing natural farming with organic farming, Dr. Hussain said natural farming can be more effective and efficient in boosting production while reducing farmers’ dependence on externally purchased inputs.The discussion also covered crop productivity, input costs, farmers’ income, water management, climate resilience and the need to make the transition towards natural farming economically viable for farmers.The special podcast series, produced by RNU Akashvani Kargil under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, will be broadcast daily at 4:30 PM from Akashvani Kargil. The programmes will also be available on the AIRNews Kargil YouTube channel.

. In line with expectations, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50 per cent, marking the first increase in the benchmark rate since February 2023.The RBI had kept the repo rate unchanged at 5.25 per cent for the past four policy reviews after cutting it by a cumulative 125 basis points in 2025.The rate hike comes amid rising retail inflation and elevated crude oil prices. The six-member Monetary Policy Committee has shifted its policy stance towards calibrated tightening.

. India’s women’s cricket captain Harmanpreet Kaur has stepped down as captain across all three formats. The 37-year-old announced her decision after a BCCI review meeting in Guwahati. Harmanpreet led India to its maiden ODI World Cup title last year and also guided the team to gold at the Asian Games. She captained India in five Tests, 51 ODIs and 155 T20Is, having led the T20 side since 2016 and taken charge of the ODI team in 2022. Harmanpreet will continue to represent India as a player across formats.

. Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey asserted that India needs capital markets that can mobilise capital, manage risk and build investor confidence.While addressing the 12th International Convention of the Commodity and Capital Market Participants Association of India in New Delhi today, he said, the regulator is working to strengthen the market structure so that households can invest with confidence, businesses can raise funds for growth, and market intermediaries maintain high standards of conduct. SEBI Chairman said, the regulator is examining concerns related to the settlement price framework for derivatives on expiry days following the introduction of the Closing Auction Session – CAS. The mechanism was introduced to improve price discovery for eligible stocks at market close by using a call-auction process to determine a single equilibrium price instead of relying solely on volume-weighted average prices.He also said, SEBI is working to deepen and improve liquidity in cash markets, expand participation and strengthen securities borrowing and lending. He added that efficient hedging and arbitrage can improve price discovery and strengthen the interaction between cash and derivatives markets. The regulator is also examining position limits for non-agricultural contracts with the aim of improving market liquidity and depth while maintaining risk controls.

. India concluded its campaign at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya with 85 medals, including 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze, finishing fourth in the overall standings. India’s 2026 Asian Games campaign produced a series of landmark achievements across disciplines.The defining feature of India’s campaign was its clean sweep of gold medals in men’s and women’s cricket, kabaddi and hockey. The Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games concluded yesterday, bringing more than two weeks of exciting sporting action to an end.In cricket, India retained both titles. The women’s team defeated Sri Lanka by 147 runs in the final, while the men’s team overcame Pakistan by 19 runs to complete the golden double.Kabaddi also produced a clean sweep. The women’s team defeated Iran 37-34 to successfully defend its title, while the men came from behind to beat Iran 40-34.Hockey also completed the sweep. The Indian women ended a 44-year wait for an Asian Games medal by defeating China 1-0, with Lalremsiami scoring the decisive goal in the 10th minute. It was India’s first women’s hockey gold at the Asian Games since 1982.The men’s team defeated Malaysia 5-1 to retain its title and claim India’s fifth men’s hockey gold, following triumphs in 1966, 1998, 2014 and 2022.It was also the first time India’s men’s and women’s hockey teams won gold at the same Asian Games. Both teams secured qualification for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics.Archery was one of India’s most successful disciplines, producing nine medals – five gold, two silver and two bronze. Boxing produced India’s best Asian Games campaign in terms of gold medals, with three gold and three bronze medals.Indian wrestlers won six medals – two gold, two silver and two bronze, making it the country’s best Asian Games wrestling tally since Jakarta 1962.

. Principal Secretary-2 to the Prime Minister, Shaktikanta Das has said that restoration of the health of the financial sector has been the defining feature of India’s resilience in recent years. He said, India’s financial sector has emerged as a strong pillar of economic growth, supported by reforms such as the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, bank recapitalization and constructive regulatory oversight. He was speaking at the Kautilya Economic Conclave 2026 in New Delhi today. Mr Das highlighted that the Gross non-performing assets have fallen sharply to 1.68 percent in June this year, while bank profitability has improved significantly. Mr Das said the prudent management of the external sector has also supported India’s efforts towards macroeconomic stability. He also mentioned that India’s external sector indicators have remained broadly resilient due to a mix of factors like the ongoing diversification of exports, conclusion of free trade agreements and sustained surplus in services trade. Mr Das said that the current account deficit for 2025-26 remained well within manageable levels at 0.6 percent of GDP.Secretary in the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Saurabh Garg, today said India’s economic resilience, supported by strong corporate performance and sustained investment activity, is now being reflected in upward revisions to the country’s growth estimates by various international agencies. Talking to the media on the sidelines of the Kautilya Economic Conclave in New Delhi, Mr. Garg said, the Indian economy had maintained its momentum after recording 7.8 per cent growth in the first quarter of the financial year 2026-27. He noted that strong corporate performance and continued capital investment, including by the private sector, were among the key indicators of the positive economic trend. He added that this momentum was also reflected in recent upward revisions to India’s growth projections by international ratings agencies and research firms, including S&P Global Ratings and Fitch Ratings.On the impact of tensions in West Asia and risks arising from global oil price shocks, Mr. Garg highlighted that government interventions, along with measures taken by households and the private sector, had helped limit the adverse impact of external shocks on the Indian economy.

. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman today said that India’s economic strength and resilience have been built over the past decade through a combination of fiscal prudence, infrastructure investment, banking reforms, improved delivery mechanisms and consistent reforms.Addressing the 5th Kautilya economic conclave in New Delhi, the Finance Minister said that the government has advanced the national frameworks through GST, insolvency and bankruptcy code and the four labour codes. She said that India had navigated the shocks of the past four years with its fundamentals intact, citing 7.8 percent real GDP growth in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026-27.The Finance Minister said that the IMF projects India’s general government debt to decline from 83.4 percent of GDP in 2026 to 77.7 percent in 2031 against a rising global trend.On infrastructure development, Ms Sitharaman said, capital expenditure for this fiscal had been budgeted at 12.22 lakh crore rupees. She added that the national highway network had expanded by about 61 per cent and the number of operational airports had more than doubled since 2014.She also highlighted that more than 52 crore collateral-free loans have been sanctioned under PM MUDRA Yojana. Highlighting the PM Awas Yojana, PM Ujjwala Yojana, Ayushman Bharat and PM Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana, Ms Sitaharaman said that these initiatives have strengthened citizens’ capacity to participate in growth and build capacities to fight the challenges.

The Ministry of Education, in coordination with the External Affairs Ministry is organizing a two day Bharat Innovates Exposition from today at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi to showcase India’s Deep-Tech innovations as a lead up to and alongside the 18th BRICS Summit 2026. The Exposition is showcasing 37 India’s Deep-Tech startups and ventures alligning with the theme of India’s BRICS Chairship Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. The event is providing participating innovators an opportunity to network with CEOs, investors, business leaders and industry representatives from BRICS member countries. Ministry of Eduaction said that the event will facilitate opportunities for Business to Business engagements, technology partnerships, investment discussions, business linkages and international market access.

. In Japan Open Tennis, world No. 3 Carlos Alcaraz will face 19th-ranked Jiri Lehecka in the Men’s Singles final in Tokyo today. Alcaraz overcame his Spanish compatriot Jaume Munar in the semifinal to prevail 5-7, 6-3, 6-1. On the other hand, Lehecka of Czech Republic defeated Monégasque Valentin Vacherot 6-4, 6-2 in the second semifinal. In Mens doubles clash, American Austin Krajicek and his Croatian partner Nikola Mektić will face French dou Théo Arribagé and Albano Olivetti in the final today.

The seven OPEC-plus countries – Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman, have decided to maintain their September 2026 production quotas unchanged for November.The decision was taken during a virtual meeting on October 4, where the countries reviewed global oil market conditions and outlook.  The group will continue to meet monthly, with the next meeting scheduled for November 1.Separately, the 68th meeting of the Joint Ministerial Monitoring Committee (JMMC) stressed the importance of protecting international maritime routes and energy infrastructure, warning that attacks or disruptions could increase market volatility and affect energy supply.

. The death toll after a Nigerian military plane flying from Benin City to Lagos crashed has climbed to 32. The 32 victims comprised 25 passengers and seven crew members. President Bola Tinubu confirmed that there were no survivors and directed the Nigerian Air Force to immediately launch a thorough investigation into the cause of the crash. According to Aviation Minister Festus Keyamo, the Air Force ATR-42 aircraft was on a routine mission yesterday when air traffic controllers lost contact with it. The wreckage was later located near the coastal town of Igbokoda in southwestern Nigeria, close to a naval base, and search and rescue teams were deployed.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over coastal and South Interior Karnataka, Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry for the next 2-3 days. The IMD said thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds may prevail over Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttarakhand, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal, Sikkim, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura tomorrow. Meanwhile, Konkan and Goa may experience Hot and Humid weather tomorrow.

. India has condemned the attack on MV ROYAD MAMMADOV in the Black Sea, in which two foreign seafarers were killed. Some members of the crew, including Indian nationals, were injured in the attack. The injured have been rescued by Romanian authorities and are receiving medical attention. The three Indian nationals, who were part crew of the ship, are safe. New Delhi has thanked Romanian authorities for their swift action in this incident.External Affairs Ministry said in a statement that India views these attacks on commercial shipping and seafarers with grave concern. It said the targeting of traffic in international waterways is severely undermining global commerce and welfare of people across the world. New Delhi continues to call for dialogue and diplomacy to bring an end to the ongoing conflicts.Earlier, in September this year, India and Liberia launched a new 25-nation “Group of Friends on Safety and Security of Shipping and Seafarers” during the UN General Assembly to ensure safety and security of merchant crews and commercial shipping against targeted attacks.

. The country’s foreign exchange reserves declined by 18.3 billion US dollars (USD) to 747.5 billion US dollars during the week ended the 25th of September. According to Reserve Bank of India data, Foreign currency assets, the largest component of the reserves, dropped by 15.5 billion USD to 615.4 billion USD during the week. Gold reserves dropped by 2.5 billion USD to 108.7 billion US dollars. Special Drawing Rights fell by 97 million USD to 18.64 billion USD. The country’s reserve position with the International Monetary Fund dipped by 86 million to 4.8 billion USD.

. The 10th edition of India Mobile Congress will begin at Yashobhoomi in New Delhi today. With the theme “Scale Without Boundaries”, it will showcase India’s remarkable progress in telecommunications, digital connectivity and technological innovation, while providing a global platform for collaboration, investment and knowledge exchange. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the event tomorrow.The event will feature the Ministerial Programme on “Investing in the Next Billion Digital Connections”, CEO Roundtable on “The Sovereign Inflection & the Future of Telecom”, AI for Good, Cyber Security Summit, 6G Symposium, Startup World Cup India 2026, ITU Build-A-Thon on AI Agents for 5G Networks, AI Safety India-UK Panel, Robotics for Youth Challenge and other global technology programmes.It will bring together over 1.5 lakh attendees, over 500 exhibitors and partners, over 600 startups and over 900 thought leaders. Over two thousand technology use cases, over 120 sessions and over 700 investor meetings will drive global collaboration and innovation.

. Tripura State Government has allotted 30.30 acres of land to the Tripura Cricket Association (TCA) for setting up a cricket academy in the state. The TCA has been asked to deposit 6 crore 81 lakh 75 thousand rupees with the Revenue Department towards the cost of the land.TCA Secretary Subrata Dey announced the development at a press conference held today at the Club House of MBB Stadium. He said, the proposed Cricket academy will be established on 30.30 acres of land in the Sekerkote area.The academy is expected to significantly benefit cricketers from across Tripura by providing them with better training and development facilities. Subrata Dey expressed hope that the land transfer process would be completed very soon.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Swiss President Guy Parmelin will address the 2nd India-EFTA Prosperity Summit, 2026, at Bharat Mandapam today, to mark the first anniversary of the India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA).The Summit will bring together senior government officials, industry leaders and key stakeholders from India and the EFTA States, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein, to further strengthen economic cooperation, foster business partnerships and unlock new opportunities in trade, investment, technology collaboration and innovation.With the theme “Building a USD 100 Billion Investment Partnership, creating 1 Million Jobs in India”, the summit will focus on reviewing TEPA progress, announcing new investments, strengthening industry-government collaboration, and exploring opportunities across key sectors. Mr Parmelin is on a three-day visit to India and the European Free Trade Association (EFTA) to mark the first anniversary of the India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA), which entered into force on October 1, 2025.Earlier, Prime Minister Narendra Modi held bilateral talks with Swiss Confederation president Guy Parmelin at Hyderabad House in New Delhi on Monday and inked several agreements in the field of promotion and collaboration on transportation technologies, mobility systems, and infrastructure. In a joint press meet, Prime Minister Modi appreciated Swiss President Guy Parmelin’s commitment to India-Switzerland relations. He said that India implemented the historic Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement with the European Free Trade Association (EFTA) last October.Speaking at the press conference, Swiss President Guy Parmelin said India-Switzerland ties were based on shared democratic values as well as on trust and mutual respect. He added that his visit is a stepping stone towards further growth, deepening and strengthening of our close, broad and long-standing partnership. He also highlighted the significance of the first anniversary of TEPA’s implementation, saying it was a moment to assess the progress made by the two sides while looking towards future cooperation.

United States, Canada and eight Latin American and Caribbean countries have accused Iran and its proxies of terrorist activities and other malign operations in the Western Hemisphere and pledged greater coordination to counter them. The joint declaration followed a US-Paraguay forum held last month to strengthen law enforcement cooperation against what Washington describes as Iranian terrorist activity in the region. The governments accused Iran and its proxies of engaging in lethal plotting, illicit fundraising, political interference and foreign influence operations across the hemisphere. The joint statement said, they stand united in determination to protect the countries and people against such threats. The statement was signed by the governments of the United States, Argentina, Canada, Colombia, Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, Guyana, Paraguay, Peru and Trinidad and Tobago.

The Government has notified the Schedule of Permissible Works under the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) [VB-G RAM G] Act, 2025, providing for 375 permissible works under the new rural works framework. The Ministry of Rural Development said the new Schedule represents a 41 percent expansion over the 266 works under the previous framework.Akashvani correspondent reports that the works have been reorganised around four thematic pillars – Water Security, Core Rural Infrastructure, Livelihood-related Infrastructure and Special Works for Extreme Weather Events and Disaster Preparedness. The Water Security pillar comprises 128 works, the highest among the four categories. It includes check dams, gully plugs, underground dykes, recharge shafts, injection wells, rejuvenation of rivers, rivulets and nallahs, reclamation of waterlogged land and renovation of field water-distribution channels.Every work will originate through a bottom-up, decentralised planning process under the Viksit Gram Panchayat Plan, approved by the Gram Sabha, and will be tracked through the Viksit Bharat National Rural Infrastructure Stack. The new Schedule seeks to align employment generation with water security, durable rural infrastructure, livelihood creation, climate resilience and inclusive development, contributing to the vision of a Viksit Bharat @2047.

The second edition of the India Art, Architecture and Design Biennale (IAADB) will be held from 4th December 2026 to 21st March 2027 in New Delhi.The theme of this 108-day Biennale is ‘Tat Tvam Asi – Reconnecting in an Age of Distraction’. Talking exclusively to Akashvani News, Secretary of the Ministry of Culture, Vivek Aggarwal said that, the Biennale will feature art installations at iconic heritage sites of the National Capital, including Purana Qila, Red Fort, Safdarjung Tomb, Qutub Minar, Qila Rai Pithora and Lodhi Garden. He said that the theme of this year’s Biennale directly takes inspiration from India’s ancient traditions and spiritual thought, which emphasize self-introspection and the unity of the individual with the larger universal consciousness.Mr Aggarwal said that the Ministry aims to take IAADB to a global level by encouraging participation from international pavilions and artists, Indian states and the private sector.Speaking about the cultural diplomacy of India, He said that cultural exchange is an important component of cultural diplomacy and the country’s soft power. Mr Aggarwal added that participation of foreign countries will provide an opportunity for Indian and international audiences to experience diverse art forms and will help position the Biennale on the global cultural calendar.Underlining the importance of Art and Design students in this Biennale, He said that the Ministry plans to involve students, particularly those pursuing art and design, in various activities associated with the Biennale, providing them opportunities to engage with artists and the wider creative ecosystem.The second edition of the India Art, Architecture & Design Biennale 2026 is the largest platform which offers artists, curators, galleries, corporates, architects, designers, cultural institutions and other stakeholders a chance to connect with culture and the creative world. This edition is conceived not as a single exhibition in a single location but as a city-wide cultural platform. Visitors will have an opportunity to experience the historical monuments along with contemporary art installations.
